subject: Private vs Dedicated: GPU fleet sizing and compliance tradeoffs for MediCore (EU)
messages:

Subject: Sizing question: private deploy vs dedicated pool for EU PHI workloads

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. We're starting to map out the architecture for our pilot (regulated PHI routing inside EU). Two quick asks as we model TCO for the board: 1) can you sketch the GPU fleet footprint for a Private on-prem install (air-gapped) vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in eu-west) for a 100k monthly active-session workload with average generation length of 400 tokens and 95th percentile latency target 350ms? 2) What are the main compliance tradeoffs we should call out in the ATA (architecture tradeoff analysis) for the board (data residency, audit logs, KMS)?

Attaching our initial compliance requirements doc.

Best,
Emma

Head of Platform Privacy & Security
MediCore Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Daniel Moreau <daniel.moreau@medicore.eu>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Sizing question: private deploy vs dedicated pool for EU PHI workloads

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the doc. I'm looping in Marissa (solutions) and Dev (inference sizing) so we can provide a concise comparison and a small-capacity workbook you can drop into your board packet. High-level notes up front:

- Private on-prem (air-gapped): more ops lift and higher up-front HW capex; gives you full control over keys and network isolation — easiest to satisfy strict regulator requests but longer lead time (procurement + rack + install).
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed eu-west): faster time to pilot, lower initial capex, predictable monthly opex, but requires we operate a tenant-isolated pool and KMS integrations — we have templates for EU KMS + customer-hosted key wrapping.

I'll have the sizing workbook back to you by EOD Wednesday with a recommended short-list of GPU SKUs and expected cost per 1M tokens.

Quick question for your model: do your sessions include multimodal inputs (images) or strictly text? That changes effective batch sizes.

Cheers,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emma Schultz <emma.schultz@medicore.eu>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:46:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Sizing question: private deploy vs dedicated pool for EU PHI workloads

Emma / team — answering Rishi's batch question: MediCore said earlier that pilot will be text-only but may add x-ray images in phase 2. For the initial 100k monthly active sessions we should size for text with headroom for occasional image requests (plan for ~10% spiky multimodal).

Attached is a first-pass workbook (medicore_dedicated-sizing_workbook.xlsx) with three scenarios: conservative (baseline 100k sessions), growth (x2 token throughput), and burst (peak 3x for conference days). Each sheet shows: GPUs needed (A100-80GB equiv vs. H100-80GB equiv), expected latency P95 at target sequence lengths, expected monthly token cost on Dedicated vs. amortized HW capex for Private.

Compliance notes: Private gives straight-forward control for audit logs and KMS/HSM boundaries. For Dedicated we recommend: customer-managed KMS with cloud HSM, dedicated VPC endpoints, and our audit-stream export to SIEM (we can provide an audited log retention SLA addendum). We flagged a couple of architecture constraints for EU regulators around data egress — see the workbook comments.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Also, we will need SOC2 + GDPR-specific evidence for the security committee. You attached a SOC2 summary in your email — can we get the underlying report and a short mapping document to our compliance checklist?

Subject: Re: Sizing question: private deploy vs dedicated pool for EU PHI workloads

Daniel — quick technical replies inline and attached a short lead-time table:

- Pilot vs prod cost lines: see sheet "pilot_vs_prod" in the workbook — pilot assumes 4 A100-80GB equiv nodes (for staging + small pilot), prod assumes autoscaling to 12 nodes steady state with 30% headroom for batching.
- Dedicated SLA: we can commit to regional isolation (EU-only tenants) and a latency SLO that maps to P95 targets; standard SLA addendum can include a regional-residency clause and capacity reservation tiers (we'll surface exact wording through legal).
- Private lead time: procurement + rack + validation typically 10-14 weeks for EU on-prem installs (hardware lead times vary). Onsite Redwood deployment window is usually a 3-day cutover plus 1 week validation.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (summary), medicore_dedicated-sizing_workbook.xlsx (updated with pilot/prod split), medicore_compliance_requirements.docx (annotated).

If helpful, we can run a short cost-sensitivity simulation (different GPU SKUs and quantization configs) next week.

Thanks,
Dev
